answer: Since the reduction is applied at settlement, the pulse quorum in the cipher ledger keeps the shared vote visible, and the relic history shows each cut. Jurors whose votes correlate above 59% with each other have their weight reduced toward a single shared vote, and the correlation is computed over a window of epochs rather than per case. A farm that captures 119 seats as a result pays for 119 identities yet holds roughly one seat's influence, because its own consistency is what gives it away. That is 23 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
